description: The analog counterpart of signoff/digital-spec.json: one entry per spec/decisions/0013-operating-conditions.md section 3 row, mapped to the sim/ testbench check that grades it or recorded as a declared gap. This file is the committed DR-0013 row-to-measure map (#372); since #229 it also sources the spec_row tags on the T1 item 5 klt sim envelopes (sim/run_envelope.py reads each row's checks per testbench), so the grader derives an envelope's row coverage from the same map. Targets, limits and statuses restate DR-0013 exactly; nothing here ratifies, relaxes or reclassifies a row. Validated by sim/tests/test_analog_spec.py, which matches every row's target text against DR-0013 section 3's own Target cell (issue #383); gap-closer liveness (every non-null closes_with still naming an open issue) is checked on demand by signoff/check_gap_issues.py.
sources: spec/decisions/0013-operating-conditions.md (Accepted) -- section 1 PVT matrix and section 3 rows
spec/decisions/0017-pll-sourcing-and-135mhz-half-rate-retarget.md (Accepted) -- the PLL is sourced from a sibling canary; row 3's end-to-end figure needs its clock

corners.matrix: DR-0013 section 1, ratified verbatim: 5 MOS process corners (tt, ff, ss, fs, sf) x {-40, 27, 125} C x {2.97, 3.30, 3.63} V (3.3 V domain, +-10 %), cross-producted with both bit rates {742.5, 270.0} Mbps/lane. res_ff/res_ss/bjt_ff/bjt_ss additionally required for any claim depending on resistor or BJT device parameters.
corners.binding: Current-mode driver rows bind at ss_-40c_2.97v or ss_125c_2.97v (DR-0013 section 1); every graded row still runs the full matrix rather than assuming it.

rows.note: swing_cmis grades the deliberate 1 pF leg-to-leg mismatch copy. AVCC-sensitivity copies (swing_avcclo/avcchi) are measured, not checked; DR-0006's supply-tracking derating is graded in design/cml-driver-sizing.md section 8.
vcm_avcclo/avcchi carry the DR-0006 supply-tracking sensitivity, measured and compared in design/cml-driver-sizing.md section 8.

rows.gap: No end-to-end measurement route: the total figure includes the PLL's jitter contribution and the PLL is outside this repository (DR-0017 -- sourced from a sibling canary; this block specifies only the interface and jitter budget it requires). This block's own contribution is row 4, which is graded below. No open issue in this repository would close this row; it lands when a PLL-model (or silicon) end-to-end jitter bench exists.

rows.note: Deterministic jitter only (ISI + rise/fall asymmetry); the realmux bench grades the harder mux-plus-driver contribution referenced to the ideal clock.

rows.target: <= 20 % of the operating UI (≈ 269 ps @ 742.5 Mbps, ≈ 741 ps @ 270 Mbps)
rows.note: The bound is rate-dependent, so the graded checks normalise the absolute trise_c*/tfall_c* measures by the measured UI (trise_c*/m_ui_ref etc.) and bound the ratio at 0.20 -- one bound correct at both rates, where a fixed absolute max would be wrong at the other. Proposed target (engineering judgement, no DVI 1.0 rise/fall citation anywhere in this repository), hence ratified: false -- grading it does not promote it. sim/tmds-final-mux-eye measures trise_m/trise_n on the mux output, not the driver pad, so it is not a row-5 bench.

rows.target: Proposed — eye height >= 50 % of the row-1 swing floor (>= 200 mV, using the 400 mV DR-0002 minimum) and eye width >= (1 − row-3's 0.25 UI budget) = >= 0.75 UI, both measured simultaneously at the eye's widest opening, no fixed sampling instant assumed
rows.note: The eyemask_margin_* checks grade height AND width together (PRBS7 pattern, every 0.75 UI window scanned). Proposed target, derived arithmetically from rows 1 and 3, hence ratified: false.

rows.target: N/A by design, not Proposed — see rationale below
rows.na_by_design: DR-0013 row 7's rationale: DR-0002's topology is current-mode open-drain, intentionally not source-matched to the receiver-side 50 ohm/leg termination, so a transmitter-reference-plane return-loss row would grade the wrong physics. The design intent is confirmed measured: ro_leg = 11.0-56.8 kOhm across the full matrix, always >= 220x the termination (design/cml-driver-sizing.md section 8, from sim/cml-driver-eye's ro_leg measure). Return loss for this channel is governed by the receiver's termination quality (off-block) and the pad/board parasitics already captured in row 5's bandwidth analysis. DR-0013 explicitly distinguishes this from Proposed (a number merely missing); whether a row no tool can evidence is a gap or something else is an operator question under the tier doc, not decided here or there.

rows.target: <= 3.63 V rated (3.3 V core devices, +10 % supply corner), positive margin required

evidence.note: The final multiplexer's own devices against the same 3.63 V rated ceiling (the bench's checks cite sim/cml-driver-eye's device-stress rows as their basis).

rows.target: 8–12 mA (this cell's own derived tolerance around the ~10 mA nominal §1 states)
rows.note: Rate-independent DC row; the 8-12 mA window is the tolerance design/cml-driver-sizing.md section 2 derives around the ~10 mA nominal.

rows.gap: No graded bench check: sim/esd-clamp-cv and sim/esd-diode-clamp-cv measure the clamp C-V per width, but their only check (cap_w444_opv) is a 50 pF broken-probe sanity ceiling, explicitly not a DR-0005/0011 compliance gate -- the <= 2 pF comparison is a design-doc computation over every corner's measured value (design/esd-capacitance-budget.md section 9: a drawn 25x25 um pad plus the ratified diode_nd2ps_06v0 clamp at 0.225-0.652 pF, cell-level PASS with 67-89 % headroom). Open legs: the pd2nw (VDD-side) clamp C-V is unmeasured since the #210 VDD-side clamp addition, and the block-level gf180_tmds_pad_ring_assembly does not yet use that pad geometry -- both under #222's re-run scope.

rows.target_supplement: (JEDEC JS-001) / (JEDEC JS-002) — the standard names DR-0013's target cell omits; they come verbatim from DR-0011, DR-0015 and spec/tmds-tx.md, and are kept outside the compared target per #383.
rows.gap: Accepted pre-silicon limitation, not schedulable work (DR-0015, which closed #145): no source in the installed gf180mcu PDK characterizes ESD failure current density, breakdown voltage, or snapback/trigger behavior for any device family, so real HBM/CDM qualification cannot happen before silicon exists. The clamp-device class is signed off (DR-0011) and the HBM sizing estimate is measured against the capacitance budget. Re-opens on real silicon/ESD-tester data or a PDK-sourced ESD electrical dataset, per DR-0015's Consequences -- no open issue in this repository would close it.
